notable_absence.finding: Encryption at rest gets an explicit performance rationale twice (native encryption at rest 'lets you fine-tune which data is encrypted... you can limit the overhead of encrypting and decrypting data'; field-level encryption framed as an alternative for the same reason), but Network Encryption's five sub-cases (node-to-node, client, console, service-port, XDCR) get no equivalent discussion of overhead anywhere on this page - an asymmetry in how thoroughly the two H2 sections were written.

cross_component_finding: encryption:system-secrets sits outside the page's own 'several options to encrypt your data at rest' framing even though passwords and certificates are exactly the kind of disk-resident, breach-exposed data that list is otherwise about - the page's own structure draws a line between 'data at rest' (the four numbered options) and 'secrets at rest' (its own separate section) without ever stating why they're organized differently. This is the page's own information-architecture choice, not an extraction artifact - flagged as-is rather than second-guessed.
cross_product_finding: Field-level encryption is documented as three separate, per-SDK-language pages (Go, Java, Python 'Encrypting Your Data'), each under its own product tree with its own independent versioning ('current' resolves differently per SDK) - the clearest evidence in this batch that field-level encryption is implemented and documented per-SDK rather than as a single cross-language server-side capability, consistent with it being framed here as something 'applications... using the SDK' do, not something Couchbase Server itself performs.
